title: Wanderings & Wonderings
subtitle: India, Burma, Kashmir, Ceylon, Singapore, Java, Siam, Japan, Manila, Formosa, Korea, China, Cambodia, Australia, New Zealand, Alaska, the States
summary: John James Aubertin (1818–1900), an Englishman known as the translator of Camoens, left London in October 1888 and came home in September 1891 after a journey round the world, and wrote this account of it for four friends. He began in India: Calcutta, Darjeeling, Burma, Benares, Bombay, Rajputana, Agra, Delhi, the Punjab, the Khyber Pass, and Kashmir, then Madras and Ceylon. He went on to Java, Siam, Hong Kong, Shanghai, and Japan, to Manila, Formosa, and Korea, and in China to Tientsin, Peking, the Ming tombs, and the Yangtze; then to Cambodia, Australia, New Zealand, Alaska, and California. He quotes much verse, and the book ends with a poem of his own to his friends. The book has a portrait and seven photographs.
